analysis: The only change in this PR is at EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift line 74. The type annotation in the tinyGemma4Text() test helper becomes the module-qualified MLXLLM.Gemma4TextConfiguration, where it was the unqualified Gemma4TextConfiguration. The edit is test-only, does not touch production source, and does not alter the JSON config or the model construction. It most likely resolves a name-ambiguity compile issue between MLXLLM and another imported or @testable module such as MLXLMCommon. Nothing here changes runtime behavior, so it adds no attack surface and invalidates no assumption in the threat model. The surrounding tests assert controls relevant to T-041 (encrypted SSD prefix cache): the fleet kill switch, the crash-loop guard, and fallback to contiguous on a failed paged preflight. They also assert the cache refusal paths and the HMAC-keyed block layouts. These assertions are unchanged and still exercise the same contracts. The tests use ephemeral keys and temporary roots, so they create no real at-rest artifacts. One residual question: the qualified type is assumed to exist in the MLXLLM module with the same decoding semantics. That is a compile-time matter and not security-relevant. I found no regressions.
